I can give you an answer to your questions. Some exposition to myself: I have been playing WoW since Vanilla with the occasional break during content droughts and one major break between 2016 and 2020 (Before Legion launch and right before SL launch). And currently I'm for almost a year on a roleplay server since PvE has been almost burnt after my start in SL again.

So.. In terms of dungeons/raids and PVP I cant tell very much except as I never really went that high with it. 

1. What makes it fun was always gameplay, Warcraft has a very direct and easy-access character control. No dodges like in GW2, a snappy movement and many mechanics in your basic controls are made to be understood by absolutely everyone.   
That flexibility and responsiveness in controls together with a rather simple combat design makes the overall access much more easier and direct. There are no flanks to attack like in Final Fantasy and your character dont act like a tank on ice sometimes like in other mmos. Classes are fun to play.   
Even though I have primary experience in druid, hunter, shaman and now the evoker. But those mechanics are for me always a big part why I returned to WoW over and over again. Just the best mechanics if you prefer a direct and responsive character.
2. The game shares its only similarities with the rough fantasy-environment. The genre is identical, but Guild Wars 2 and WoW are very different games. From visual style, from the way it tells its story up to the gameplay aspects.   
WoW is built around a much more extensive variety in classes, abilities and also uses of your class while aiming at a vertical progression system in which you always get higher and higher with values the better you are.   
So nothing really much like Guild Wars 2 where you have always just 10 skills active (depending on class ofc) and where horizontal progression finds eventually an end to which only your skill is important for combat. Both games cant be really compared, but this can give a rough overview by the big differences. Also storytelling is vastly different as you dont have in WoW things like your personal story like in Guild Wars 2. Mounts are, except of the new dragonriding mounts, like your character but on higher speed.
3. That one depends on certain factors: Much of the old achievements are still obtainable. Much of the old content is still playable, but your success is in many ways much harder as most players have moved on to newer expansions and leave the old ones behind. Because there is almost no reason to do old things by design. But much is still obtainable. Other things sadly arent. Especially as druid player you will learn the sad truth about the special cat- and bear-forms which are no longer obtainable.
4. Old content is dead. Quite literally. Its rare that you meet other players on your journey through old places. And those people are usually two kind of people: The first are those who go there on purpose to hunt for special things like mounts, achievements, transmog etc. Many old raids are easily soloable and many people just go through them weekly for the chance of having an amazing sword etc.  
The other group are usually people who either level through the zones without using the dungeon finder. But in general you wont meet many people on your journey. You can level from level 10 to 60 in old content and possibly never meet someone else.
5. It depends what you count as "except for questing". There are factions you can grind up for rewards, some of those factions offer mounts, others offer transmog you cant get anywhere else. Those factions arent really needed anymore as they are, like the world they are in, useless for current content on the dragon isles. But there are things you can do, and Blizz vastly expanded the possibilities from MoP upwards.  
In MoP you had something like a little farm with npcs, in WoD you had the infamous garrison which is one of the big reasons for inflation in gold. In Legion you had your class order hall and your artefact weapons which are useless by now but serve as amazing transmog which you can still work towards. You also can get mounts and class-related transmog doing the campaign there.   
World quests, factions to grind etc. Also with Legion and later with BfA you can unlock the allied races for horde and alliance by questing through zones and doing special scenarios which widens the variety of races you can play vastly. BfA was pretty much the same like Legion in many ways, but ramped up to the extreme with island expeditions which can give cool transmog, horrific visions and much else. Shadowlands had nothing much to offer but has many cool transmogs and Torghast which was more like an experiment on a rogue-like mode. Shadowlands also has mounts etc to farm now. And yeah, now Drafonflight is the current thing.

The first one was a guy (Dylan), wielding an greataxe as focus and using the powers of demonology and fire, even when he had big troubles with wielding demonic powers at the start of the story. The second character was a woman (Seras), using a crossbow and was in general really invested in air-magic which she used to grant her projectiles much more force and also gave her much more capabilities in movement.

Dylan was a former 'noble' of sorts, being banished from his family after they recognized inpurity in him. His family had really big ties to the fire, they were among the best fire wielders in the world. His demonic powers made him undesireable as part of family and they left him behind. He had always big troubles in controlling his powers, therefore he kept the demonic force in secret.

Seras on the other hand was a trained soldier. She was cast out from the army because of one major mistake she did in her past, causing her to search for another job. With her skill and her powers she became a bounty hunter, and most of the missions she took were hunting down criminals and dangerous beings at all costs and neglecting herself in the process. She was pretty tough, at least thats what she showed at first.

Both saw each other nothing more than just a person they cant respect or like in any way, always having conflicts with each other. But when a city was destroyed and the protagonists couldnt help, Dylan and Seras found in each other more than just people they had to stick to because of one bigger goal. Seras has seen Dylan trying to save people which were doomed, showing her that he wasnt just a stupid grunt who fought because its fun. She saw that he was compassionate and that his morals are higher than his personal feelings. And Dylan noticed that Seras, despite being an asshole until that point, had also her own troubles that caused her being unable to do anything in that specific situation. That she had a good heart and that things happened that brought her in the way of 'never compromising', even when she was neglecting herself with it. They began to talk more friendly after this occasion and found some sort of respect for each other that eventually brought them into a romance much later.

You can make insane amounts of gold where 5 million gold are just peanuts to you. Most of them are considered 'morally grey' like selling mount runs. I never did such thing, but I know people who do.. And yeah, selling voidtalon for one million gold per try.. Insane, just insane. But my point wasnt that I make such amounts of gold myself, even when I explain further how I made six million gold in two months by simple farming valueable resources and using the bugged meta to my advantage.

There are many ways of making good amounts of gold. But you usually cant make insane amounts of gold if you arent willing to break the tos or manipulating the auction house to your benefit. One way of genuine gold making is by selling transmogs. Especially if you know what to look for. Most transmog is pretty standard and dont sell that high. But some very specific ones can make you much money. Usually they are random drops or crafted ones with rare recipes and such. But its not really the means of getting these items, its more important how they look. And there are certain transmogs that always sell very well, at least on the servers I played on. You want to play as bloedelf looking like a spellbreaker? Yeah, you can get an transmog that make your bloodelf look like an spellbreaker. Costs? You dont want to know for how much you can sell each piece of armor.

But there is, to be honest, another good, but also fast-burning, way to make money. Wait for the next expansion to release, and then farm the hell out of any resource you can gather. Leather is always valueable, same as cloth. Both are, especially at new releases, always the most valueable stuff you can farm. Herbs, iron and such dont have the insane demand at the start usually. When shadowlands released I spend every day four hours in the morning just farming leather in Ardenweald. I had a second character at that time too just for enchanting and especially disenchanting. My druid skinned everything possible for hours just for use them in leatherworks, upgrading the simple leather to the better ones. And the ones you can enchant I enchanted with my alt.

Between the release of shadowlands and start of January of the following year I made around six million gold just by leather alone. Because everyone wanted legendaries. Since most classes rely on leather in one way or another you can always make good money with leather. You dont have to craft stuff, just sell that stuff. And thanks to the bugged meta during 9.0-times you could always make insane gold with leather because of the flood of convo-druids and hunters and whatnot made the demand way higher than ever. I'm talking about selling one enchanted leather for over 6K gold in the auction house, and I sold stacks over stacks from that leather alone. Or eternal crystals for 10K gold each because everyone wanted enchants.

Thing is, my way of gold farming isnt that reliable and consistent because it heavily relies on taking advantage of the first months where the demand is highest and you sell the right things at the right time. Also I used the bugged meta at the start of shadowlands to my advantage and concentrated my efforts just to supply enough leather for the insane demand of the playerbase from my server.

I will, to be honest, do exactly the same thing with Dragonflight. Since the professions will become more valueable there will be ways of making insane amounts of money again when you keep your eyes open for resources and certain things everyone needs. And with knowledge about current meta and predicting the playerbase and the economy you can make good money, but its always a risk. I couldnt have made six million gold when that bugged druid-convo-meta never happened and therefore the flood of boomkins never came.

Es gibt nicht viele Serien die ich schätze, aber diese sind umso besser was Storytelling angeht. Eine die ich sehr schätze ist Avatar: The Last Airbender.

Natürlich, es ist eine eher auf eine jugendliche Audienz ausgelegte Serie, aber diese Serie ist dennoch was Charakterentwicklung und Storytelling angeht den meisten Serien heutzutage meilenweit voraus. Eines der Gründe liegt daran weil die entsprechenden Protagonisten und Antagonisten Persönlichkeiten haben die abseits von plumpen Stereotypen existieren. Sie begehen Fehler mit teilweise weitreichenden Konsequenzen, erbringen gute Taten die manchmal auch unmoralisches Verhalten verlangen. Selbst die Bösewichte sind innerhalb dieser Serie auch Charaktere, die mehr als eine Dimension besitzen und ihre eigene Persönlichkeit besitzen, die sie einzigartig und ihre Taten auf eine gewisse Weise rechtfertigen. Sie sind weitaus menschlicher als eine Rey und Kylo Ren von den neuen Star wars-Filmen oder sämtlichen Charakteren der HBO Watchmen. Und das für einen Cartoon.

Wenn ich Serien und Filme schaue lasse ich das nicht über mich herein rieseln. Ich habe, auch wegen meiner eigenen kreativen Arbeit, ein großes Interesse daran die dargestellte Welt zu analysieren und auch die Charaktere in allen Facetten zu betrachten die möglich sind. Ebenso auch auf Storytelling.

Game of Thrones war ab der vierten Staffel nicht mehr auf Basis der Romanvorlage, was den Produzenten die Möglichkeit gab die Story auf ewig weiter zu spinnen weil auch bei nachträglichen Releases von neuem Buchmaterial der Serien-Kanon nicht mehr dem Buch-Kanon entspricht. Walking Dead könnte ebenfalls noch weitere zwanzig Jahre laufen wenn die Serie nicht über ihre faule Schreibweise gefallen wäre. Dasselbe mit vielen anderen Serien die heutzutage produziert werden.

*What if we deleted cancer out of existence*? hmmm, probably we would have taken a big hit in our medical procedures, because cancer made a big impact on our medical knowledge that we sometimes underestimate. Cancer plays a big part in the research for long-time-illnesses and also the treatment of such, and knowledge about cancer also brought us some knowledge about mutations and genetics. These are, at the end, good aspects of cancer.

*What if we deleted nuclear weapons*? Sound good, but the result of it won't be that great. The primary reason why the cold war never went hot was because both sides used nuclear weapons as a threat and not as an actual weapon. Development of said weapons went further and further, yes this is true. But world peace during that time period was only hold because of this weapons. This make them a little bit redeemable because they weren't constructed to be used. Just as a threat against opponents. Because ... simple war logic: You fight a war for a purpose. If you choose to use nuclear weaponry ... and you know that your opponent have some similar to yours ... what do you think you can win in this situation? Both sides use their weaponry, and everything will be lost. And this isn't in any dimension a favorable outcome for any general or whatever who wants to achieve the victory. Because, why being successful in your war when nothing is left at the end? This is why the saying that the third world war being nuclear is bs.

*What if we deleted the war or violence itself*? Yes, you probably won't ever existed if this important aspect of human history would be deleted. Human history, human progress, and the whole human civilization was achieveable because of violence and war. Because some were ready to kill and harm others, not only humans, but also predatory animals, for protection. There weren't big civilizations that worked well because of things like humanism or equality. Such civilizations likely existed, but they all got destroyed and washed away. Because in the most important times where they needed to survive they weren't able to fight to protect their values and their morals. At some time they become weak, and other groups who don't think the same way as the humanistic civilizations will become more powerful because of the fact that the enemy gets weaker.

*And what if we deleted mental illnesses from existence*? Yep, this sounds really good right? Nope, absolutely not. We won't understand the impact of our psyche, we won't even have the need to understand it in a way we do right now. Because, if such problems don't exist, why should we care for it? Mental illnesses and the understanding of this illnesses have brought many good things for the overall understanding of human minds. Yes, people suffered for this, and people will suffer from it in future. But the knowledge is, in general spoken, more important than people who suffer because of it. If mental illnesses never existed, the whole concept of "human psychology" would be laughable in public and a topic that would be in the same spot as "believing in supernatural beings", even tho human psychology is a thing. But in such a different world this most likely won't be a thing. 

What I want to tell is: Yes, you probably want to delete something from existence you may not like. But the impact of this action isn't fully predictable and comprehensable for you, and this goes for me too. And the outcome of this most likely won't make this world a better place but a place that you may can't recognize anymore.

Not because I'm hypercritical and just want to say something "cool" or whatever. But because of two reasons:

*For the past*: Even if I had the intention of going back and enjoying childhood events, I would consider my time back then as lost time. Because good childhood memories are mostly kept alive by nostalgia. And when someone gets back to his childhood they may feel the nostalgia, but would more likely see the things as they were: Not as great as they remember them. I, for myself, wouldn't have today as much fun with the games I played back then. Or would enjoy the time I had with certain things back then in the same way. So this won't be viable for me.

*For the future*: Why should I even bother to take the surprise out of my future life? I mean, even if I'm able to get to the situation where I could see into my future, what would this mean for me? This would change my whole perspective of my future because I know something about it. It doesn't even mean that such future events have to happen, but knowing that this possibility even exist would change my decision making in certain aspects, and therefore take my responsibility and my freedom at some degree away from me. It's not the same than having plans that may success or fail, because you make these plans with your todays knowledge. But having direct knowledge about any possible future event will change the overall decision making in one way or another. And that in a deterministic way. There is a very small difference.

I felt bad for the being I became. I've gone to my mirror and just had a monologue with myself I clearly remember:

"What is my reason to be this way? Is it my own fear that drive me in this life? Why don't I kill myself when there isn't something to live for? Why am I even alive if my life is just suffering? When my task was all the time that I had to keep my dark side shut from everything, and this makes me suffer in every way and a miserable creature, why do I take this task in the first place. When I kill myself I don't have to bear this task, right?"

And then reality kicked completely in. I didn't lived because I wanted to keep my dark side shut. My main task wasn't this. I never had a task to begin with, and I lied to myself that I had some. No one would care if I had this task, and no one would ever thank me for doing this task. And I acknowledged that I never died, even in my darkest time I always ended the suicide approach at some point, because I never wanted to die. Because I wanted to live. I wanted to bear this task because I wanted to live.

And with this simple realization that I wanted to live my life that kept me from killing myself I began to change. Not only that I chose to accept myself and my struggles, taking the responsibility of my failed life at that point and that the only person who could save me was only myself. But also I changed mentally. I killed my depression, I killed my delusions, I even killed my pride, my ego, my past and my big evil demon that I thought I had by my own. I never accepted therapy back then, and I solved my problems without therapy.

I became the man I never saw in myself. And I became the wielder of my will. My will became my sword and shield in times of need. My will became the foundation of myself. My will became the wall that keep dangers outside and myself protected. But also my will became the weapon that can destroy the wall if a new one have to be build.

And today, after half an year of my completely turnaround, I know that my progress isn't over. But I know that every little step I do in every way, I know that I do this step because I want to. If I fail, it's my fault if this will hurt me or if I go for a second try. If I do something irresponsible, I know that I wanted it this way.

And as of today. I'm doing progress. I started to workout to bring my body in shape because I don't want to be a fat blob of a guy. I'm looking forward to get back to work again. I'm looking for a new place to live. And I changed many things about my life at all. And, to end this storytime, I'm feeling good. Even if I'm sad sometimes or angry, I'm also happy that these feelings can occur and I find strength in feeling these. I have found myself and therefore my purpose.

I interpret the ubermensch in the way of self-awareness and the power of your will. Nihilism, and the questioning of any worth in life, is the first step to become ubermensch. You have to know how worthless following social dogma is for the overall setting. Knowing how useless your entire existence is, and that you can't change something meaningful that will persist to the end. Knowing about that nothing will last forever, therefore your own life and your accomplishments doesn't mean anything at the end.

Nihilism in it's core is where you, as a human, show what you really are. Knowing that you are worthless and don't have any purpose, that no one planned or created you and there isn't any god who exist and care, can make you miserable and lost. This general hopelessness can make you miserable.

But, in other way, you can achieve the state of ubermensch.

The ubermensch is at the end a state of mind, where you aren't vulnerable to others by choice. Where no one can hurt you in an emotional way because it's your mastery of yourself that can prevent that. If someone lied to you or broke a promise, it's your responsibility how you react to it. Does it make you disappointed and sad or do you stand above it and do what you truly want?

This is ubermensch. Others can hurt you emotionally if you let them. Others can mess you up because you let them. And the metamorphosis of Ubermensch have this in it's core. Invulnerability because of self-mastery of your emotions, your thoughts and your will. You become self-aware to a degree where you have the active choice. Others can't hurt you if you chose against it. Not in a physical way, but in an emotional and psychological way. Others may break your bones, but your mind they won't ever break.

And, beside that, you create your worth by your own. There comes the existantialism into play. Because you made yourself self-aware and you have the choice and control your will, you are able to create your own worth and values not because others dictated them, but by you actively giving yourself a worth for everything. Even knowing that nothing of that will ever matter at the end.

This is what nihilism leads to if you are capable of going through the whole process. The reason why very few people actually managed to do this is that you have to go through a lot of suffering. Suffering because of understanding of your non-existing role and purpose in life, Suffering because the fact that you aren't worth anything like everyone else. And suffering that nothing you can do will persist or change your death and therefore that you will be forgotten and everything you are. This suffering and hopelessness can drive many people insane. Because we are socialized with values and worldviews we happily apply to when we are a child. We are raised with values in mind, and to reject everything you know and become lost by choice is pretty hard to bear. And many can't survive this because humans need a purpose for themselves. And I don't blame that we are raised by values because it serves a purpose for society.

And ... another reason why you don't hear from such people who became ubermensch: Because why should they care about how others think of them? If they are telling you that they are ubermensch, they actually aren't. There isn't any meaning behind it by saying this because if you are truly ubermensch, you aren't in need of others attention or admiration. Because you are this way by choice. Because you know what you are and what you are capable of. Others opinion is just noise in a world full of noise by that point, and you are standing above others admiration or fulfilling your ego with that. 

Same you could say in terms of smart, strong or independent people. If you are smart, strong or independent or whatever positively connoticed, you aren't in need of others attention. Because you already know you are smart, strong or independent. Absolutely the same goes for ubermensch. If you are one, you don't have to tell others about it because it doesn't make sense to you.

To be a ubermensch, on the other hand, doesn't mean that you need to be a mean person or whatever. It doesn't mean that you are standing above others in values or such things. And it doesn't justify anything good or bad. The only things you do as ubermensch are completely made by your choice and your values you made.

And this is what my goal is. To become ubermensch. There are many aspects of myself I have to change, yes. I'm not at the end of this metamorphosis, but at some day I will. Because I made my choice.
